title: The ocean's plastic smog
text: If you sailed to the Great Pacific Garbage Patch you would not find a floating island of bottles, because the plastic there has weathered {{1}} finely that neither nets nor satellites can easily map it. {{2}} is the great rotating currents, the gyres, {{3}} quietly gather drifting rubbish towards their calm centres. Pieces range {{4}} bottle caps and fishing floats to fibres thinner than sewing thread, and sunlight eventually breaks each item {{5}} countless microplastics that sink, suspend or drift at every depth. There is {{6}} simple clean-up, and engineers struggle precisely {{7}} the fragments are so small and so widely scattered. What the patch offers instead is a lesson: {{8}} we burn, bury or recycle matters less than not throwing the past century's convenience into the sea in the first place.

gaps.explanation: 'So finely that' — degree plus result clause.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ is the great currents that
gaps.explanation: The cleft structure emphasises the currents.
Non-defining relative after the pair of commas.

gaps.hint: preposition: range ___ bottle caps to fibres
gaps.explanation: 'Range from X to Y' — the first element takes 'from'.
Change of state ending inside takes 'into'.
'No' negates the noun; 'not' cannot precede 'simple clean-up'.

gaps.hint: conjunction: ___ we burn, bury or recycle
gaps.explanation: Fronted subject clause with alternatives: whether.
